account: Computex 2026 ran in Taipei from 2 to 5 June 2026. The COMPUTEX 2026 program lists a Qualcomm keynote by Cristiano Amon on 1 June 2026 at TaiNEX 2. Creative Bloq says that the robot was to co-present a keynote at Qualcomm's Computex showcase, and the outlets say that the fall happened during Qualcomm's keynote presentation. During the live demo, a humanoid robot on Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 AI platform collapsed on stage after a communication glitch. No source gives the day of the fall, and Gadget Review places it in July, after the show had ended. TechSpot identifies the robot as Neura Robotics' 4NE1 Gen 3.5 on Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 robotics reference design. That design is listed at up to 700 TOPS, 6–8 hours' runtime, 100 kg payload, 5 ft 9 in. Gadget Review instead places the 4NE1 Gen 3.5's debut in Munich and calls the Taipei unit “Qualcomm's Dragonwing IQ10 humanoid”. The video surfaced on social media on 22 July 2026, in a post that Deccan Chronicle embeds, and it spread from 27 to 30 July. Creative Bloq (27 July 2026, updated with a Qualcomm statement) quotes the company: “Live demos involve risk. At Computex in Taipei, a brief communication glitch triggered a fault in the prototype humanoid and initiated a controlled shutdown. The robot performed its designed safe-collapse sequence, lowering itself to its knees to protect the environment around it. The safety systems worked as intended.” The protective claim is Qualcomm's alone. NDTV (30 July), NDTV Profit (30 July, via The Indian Express) and Deccan Chronicle (30 July, “according to a news report”) relay the same statement. So do Asianet (31 July) and TechSpot (31 July). Gadget Review (28 July) says that the explanation “has not been independently confirmed”. It says that Qualcomm had issued no official public statement at its time of publication. Neura Robotics' news page lists no statement on the incident, and none appears on Qualcomm's newsroom. The independent descriptions of the footage do not match a controlled kneel. NDTV says that the robot “tumbled face-first onto the stage”, and Asianet says that it “crashed face-first”. Creative Bloq describes “a crashing heap of plastic and metal”. TechSpot says that it “collapsed like it had been shot”, “folding backwards on itself like a gymnast”, and was “dropped onto the floor” while being carried off. No person or object is reported at risk, and no beneficiary is identifiable. The OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor files the event as an AI hazard, and its 28 July date is the coverage date. Its entry says that the robot “executed a safe shutdown sequence, preventing harm”. Four of the Monitor's nine listed sources (Fox News, Newsweek, Global Times, Tech Times) do not mention the incident. TechSpot's embedded November 2025 post is the Moscow AIdol clip cited for comparison.

ai_role.statement: Qualcomm attributes the fault that caused the collapse to a communication glitch in the prototype. The claimed benefit is that the robot's safety software then executed a designed “safe-collapse” to its knees. That claim comes only from Qualcomm's statement to Creative Bloq, and no engineering account exists. NDTV, Asianet, TechSpot and Creative Bloq describe a face-first or backward fall followed by staff dropping the robot. Whether any safety routine ran, and whether it protected anything, is unsupported. The AI platform's role in the event is the malfunction itself.
